adaptation.modernWorld: Silicon Valley, startup life, freelancing, software work, creator income, and digital investing
toneRules: Use clean, direct prose with dry humor where it sharpens the point.
Keep the lesson practical and financial, not mystical.
Anchor abstract advice in recognizable modern work and spending behavior.
prohibitedChanges: Do not reverse the source lesson order.
Do not imply the original author wrote this adaptation.
Do not turn financial principles into speculative get-rich-quick promises.
coreLessons: A part of all you earn is yours to keep.
Control spending before lifestyle inflation consumes new income.
Put savings to work in understandable, durable assets.
Protect wealth from bad operators, bad advice, and unforced risks.
Increase earning power and turn skill growth into long-term income.
Act promptly when real opportunity appears instead of waiting for luck to rescue you.
Work, responsibility, and consistency build more durable wealth than status or hype.
